newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends up but off highs after data.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends up but off highs after data.

text.p: The key December Euroyen futures contract ended firmer but off earlier highs hit after surging on weaker-than-expected industrial production data on Thursday, and traders said the downside is growing increasingly solid.
April industrial output fell 0.4 percent from the previous month, against earlier forecasts of a 0.3 percent rise.
The December settled at 98.86 after briefly rising by 0.1 from Wednesday's settlement to 98.89 after the data came out.
It moved from 98.75 to 98.89, with a volume of 150,498.

"There was some concern earlier that the U.S. and Japan might carry out a joint interest rate rise in July, but these industrial production figures erased that worry and set off buying," one city bank trader said.
Another trader said the topside was likely to become heavy near 98.90 on profit-taking, at least over the next few days, while the downside will grow solid near 98.75.
"Since predictions of output for the April-June quarter and June are not so good, it will be difficult to sell December until the tankan comes out in late June," he added.

The Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said industrial output in the April-June quarter was expected to fall 0.7 percent quarter-over-quarter but rise 6.1 percent year-on-year. A 1.9 percent fall has been forecast for June.

An announcement on Wednesday that the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s "tankan" business survey would be released on June 25 had put futures under selling pressure in morning trade, although the BOJ had said this did not signal any change in monetary policy.
Trade for the rest of this week is likely to be quiet, with December hovering near 98.85 and activity mainly confined to book-squaring, one trader said.

Key overnight call money was traded at around 0.50 percent against Wednesday's 0.52 percent as a result of an accommodative money market operation by the BOJ, which injected a net 100 billion yen into the market against a shortfall of 10 billion yen. This was the first such operation by the BOJ since May 9.
Although three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were offered at 0.60 percent, no trade was made. Around 120 billion yen of CDs were issued at 0.60 percent on Wednesday.
Interest rate swaps slipped after an initial morning rise, with the two-year rate quoted at 1.40/1.44 percent against 1.45/1.49 percent on Wednesday.
